vertical.caption: young duke
vertical.edit: Same scene, same crown, ermine cape and quad bike in the mud, but the rider is the same man at about twenty: smooth face, no beard, thick dark hair under the crown, the same wide-open shout.

vertical.caption: duke and duchess
vertical.edit: An elderly duchess in a tiara, pearls and a long ball gown sits behind him on the quad bike, clinging to his cape and shrieking as the mud sprays up her dress.

horizontal.caption: to bow to the duke
horizontal.edit: A line of household staff (butler, maids, gardener) stands on the lawn beside the puddle, all bowing deeply at the waist as he roars past and mud splashes their backs.

horizontal.caption: to serve the duke
horizontal.edit: A butler in tailcoat runs beside the quad bike holding out a silver tray with a teacup and teapot; the duke reaches for the cup with one hand while steering through the mud.

horizontal.caption: to photograph the duke
horizontal.edit: A crowd of tourists at the edge of the field points big cameras at him, flashes going off, while he poses mid-splash. Cameras without logos or brand names.

question: What is the duke doing?
answerWhy: Matches the clip: he drives across the field into the muddy puddle, which sprays up in the still; present continuous for the action, B-level vocabulary (quad bike, puddle), 9 words.
notes: Image pilot, 6 images in total. Each caption has one unique visual marker so a learner can match at a glance: young face / a second rider in a tiara / people bowing / silver tea tray / cameras and flashes; the original is 'old duke'. Dropped 'duke's castle' (the stately home is already in the original, so it cannot be told apart) and 'to meet the duke' (a handshake reads like greeting or serving). 'to serve' and 'to bow to' both use staff, but bowing bodies vs a held-out tea tray are separable.
